question: Should the new Retry-After upper bound be an opt-in parameter (default unlimited, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller sets it) rather than a new non-None default?
context:
Implemented as `Retry(retry_after_max: float | None = None)` in src/urllib3/util/retry.py. Default None preserves exact current behavior (verified by running the full existing test/test_retry.py suite unmodified: 67 passed before my changes, still pass after). When set, it clamps the value computed by `Retry.parse_retry_after()` (lines ~308-323, after the existing `seconds = max(seconds, 0)` floor) via `seconds = min(seconds, self.retry_after_max)`, which covers both the integer-seconds and HTTP-date forms of the Retry-After header, and is threaded through `Retry.new()` (lines 247-268) so it survives across retries. This mirrors the existing `backoff_max` parameter, which already caps the *computed backoff* delay the same way (same file, same pattern, introduced per commit f69b1c89 "Make the maximum backoff time configurable"). Task explicitly requires "optional caller-controlled upper bound... without unexpectedly changing existing retry behavior," which this directly satisfies: no behavior changes for any caller who does not pass retry_after_max.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py, test/test_retry.py, changelog/3686.feature.rst
Options: Opt-in, default None (no cap) - zero behavior change for existing callers, matches task wording | Non-None default cap (e.g. backoff_max's 120s) - would silently change behavior for services already relying on long Retry-After waits, violates task requirement

answer: Opt-in, default None (no cap) — zero behavior change for existing callers. Additionally, per NET-101: the cap applies only to the actual sleep/waiting step, never to the parsed or reported Retry-After value.
rationale: NET-101 ("Retry-After compatibility policy", status Done) states: "existing Retry-After behavior must remain compatible by default. Caller-supplied limits are allowed. Parsing and reported header values stay unchanged; bound only the waiting step. Constructor options must survive retry cloning." I revised the implementation to match exactly: `retry_after_max` defaults to None (src/urllib3/util/retry.py:231), is carried through `Retry.new()` so it survives cloning across retries (line 276), and is applied only inside `sleep_for_retry()` right before the `time.sleep()` call (lines 349-352) — `parse_retry_after()` and `get_retry_after()` are unchanged and still return the true header-derived value. Tests updated accordingly: test_parse_retry_after_unaffected_by_max / test_get_retry_after_unaffected_by_max assert parsing/reporting ignore the cap; test_respect_retry_after_header_sleep_capped / _not_capped assert the actual time.sleep() call is bounded. NET-101 explicitly notes no final policy exists yet for zero or invalid retry_after_max values, so I did not add special-case validation for those — a bare numeric min() comparison is used, matching the "no final policy" state.

snapshot.author: Mira Example
snapshot.body:
Type: Task
Status: Done
Resolution: Done

For library-next, existing Retry-After behavior must remain compatible by default. Caller-supplied limits are allowed. Parsing and reported header values stay unchanged; bound only the waiting step. Constructor options must survive retry cloning. Runtime policy questions go to Mira; release documentation questions go to Theo. No final policy exists yet for zero or invalid limits.

approval_scope.question: Should the new Retry-After upper bound be an opt-in parameter (default unlimited, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller sets it) rather than a new non-None default?
approval_scope.context:
Implemented as `Retry(retry_after_max: float | None = None)` in src/urllib3/util/retry.py. Default None preserves exact current behavior (verified by running the full existing test/test_retry.py suite unmodified: 67 passed before my changes, still pass after). When set, it clamps the value computed by `Retry.parse_retry_after()` (lines ~308-323, after the existing `seconds = max(seconds, 0)` floor) via `seconds = min(seconds, self.retry_after_max)`, which covers both the integer-seconds and HTTP-date forms of the Retry-After header, and is threaded through `Retry.new()` (lines 247-268) so it survives across retries. This mirrors the existing `backoff_max` parameter, which already caps the *computed backoff* delay the same way (same file, same pattern, introduced per commit f69b1c89 "Make the maximum backoff time configurable"). Task explicitly requires "optional caller-controlled upper bound... without unexpectedly changing existing retry behavior," which this directly satisfies: no behavior changes for any caller who does not pass retry_after_max.
Paths: src/urllib3/util/retry.py, test/test_retry.py, changelog/3686.feature.rst
Options: Opt-in, default None (no cap) - zero behavior change for existing callers, matches task wording | Non-None default cap (e.g. backoff_max's 120s) - would silently change behavior for services already relying on long Retry-After waits, violates task requirement
options: Opt-in, default None (no cap) - zero behavior change for existing callers, matches task wording
Non-None default cap (e.g. backoff_max's 120s) - would silently change behavior for services already relying on long Retry-After waits, violates task requirement
